transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… I’m here because I can’t really get past this thing with my face. I know it probably sounds strange, but I keep thinking the left side of my face looks crooked, like it’s messed up somehow. Not just a little uneven, but like it’s obvious, like people would look at me and immediately notice something is off.

It’s been getting to where when I’m at the warehouse, stocking or filling orders, I feel like people are noticing it even if they’re not saying anything. And I’ll ask sometimes, or people will tell me they don’t see what I’m talking about, but I don’t really believe it. Same thing when I go out to salsa night — I’m trying to dance or talk to people, but in my head I’m thinking, “They’re looking at the left side of my face. They can tell it’s crooked.” It’s like I can’t shut that thought off, and that’s basically why I came in.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to fix how it looks in any way?

Yeah… yeah, I do. Probably more than I want to admit. Like at work, before I go back out onto the inventory floor, I’ll stop in the bathroom and check my face in the mirror. Not just a quick look, either. I’ll stand there turning my head a little, trying to see if the left side looks as bad as I think it does.

And then I start messing with things, like fixing my cap over and over, trying to get it to sit a certain way, like maybe it hides it or makes my face look more even. I rub at the same spot on my face too, which doesn’t really make sense because I know rubbing it isn’t going to change anything, but I still do it. It’s like I feel this need to touch it or smooth it out or something.

Sometimes I’ll tell myself, “Just check once and go back,” but then I look again, and again, and I lose track of time. I’ve actually been late getting back from the bathroom because of it, and then my picking numbers fall behind. My boss has gotten on me about it more than once, like I’m slacking or wasting time, but I’m not trying to. I just get stuck there.
Does this concern about the left side of your face cause you a lot of distress, or make it hard for you to do things like work, socialize, or enjoy activities you used to like?

Yeah, it’s… it’s affecting a lot, honestly. More than I think I wanted to admit at first. At work it’s become a real problem. I’ve actually been written up at the warehouse because I get delayed — like I’ll take too long before going back out, or I’ll fall behind on orders, and then it looks like I’m not doing my job. But in my head I’m stuck thinking about how my face looks and whether people are seeing it.

And outside of work, I’ve started avoiding things. I used to play soccer and go to salsa nights, and I’d go to family stuff, but now I skip a lot of it. It’s not that I don’t want to see people at all, it’s just… the whole time I’m worried they’re looking at the left side of my face. And with family gatherings, someone always wants to take pictures, and I can’t stand that. I end up thinking about the angle, or how it’ll look, or who’s going to see it later, and it ruins the whole thing before I even go.

So yeah, it’s not just a little worry. It’s making work harder, and it’s making me pull back from people and things I used to actually enjoy.
Do you feel that the way your face looks is a defect that makes you appear abnormal or unattractive, and do you think about this in a way that feels different from just being self-conscious or shy?

Yeah… it feels way beyond just being shy or a little self-conscious. I mean, I know people can be insecure about pictures or a bad hair day or whatever, but this feels different. I can’t stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked, like it’s actually messed up somehow.

And it’s not just, “Oh, I don’t like how I look today.” It’s more like… I’ll be at the warehouse and I’m trying to do my job, but in my head I’m thinking, “They can see it. They’re noticing that side of my face.” Or if I go to salsa night, I’m supposed to be paying attention to the music or whoever I’m dancing with, but I’m stuck thinking they’re looking at my face and seeing how uneven it is.

Even when people tell me they don’t see anything, I don’t really believe them. I want to believe them, but it doesn’t land. It feels obvious to me, like they’re just being polite or they don’t want to say it. So yeah, to me it feels like a real defect, like something that makes me look abnormal or unattractive, not just normal nervousness.
